cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: kube-apiserver is the front door of Kubernetes. Every request from kubectl, Helm, controllers, the scheduler and kubelets goes through it, and nothing except the API server talks directly to etcd. A central API avoids a mesh of point-to-point integrations, each with its own security and validation.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Each request passes a pipeline: accept over HTTPS, authenticate, authorize, admission control, validate, then persist to etcd. The API server holds no state of its own; etcd is the source of truth, which is why several API server replicas can run behind a load balancer for high availability.

questions.q: Which component is the only one allowed to talk to etcd directly?
questions.a: kube-apiserver. All other components read and write cluster state through it.

questions.q: List the request pipeline stages in order.
questions.a: Accept the request, authentication, authorization, admission control, validation, then persist to etcd.
questions.hint: Who, may they, should it, is it valid, save

questions.q: Why can kube-apiserver run active-active behind a load balancer?
questions.a: It is stateless. All state lives in etcd, so any replica can serve any request.
